REQ-API-001 Business routes share the versioned base Tested 3/3 covered

Every business route SHALL be served under /api/v1. The liveness probe and the documentation routes SHALL sit outside that base. The published document SHALL declare the base once in its server entry and SHALL declare its paths relative to it.

REQ-API-002 Requests carry business data only Tested 4/4 covered

A request body SHALL be application/json and SHALL carry business data. A missing or unsupported media type SHALL answer 415 Unsupported Media Type, an unparseable body 400 Bad Request, and a body whose shape or values fail a schema, framing or business rule 422 Unprocessable Content. A hypermedia member in a request SHALL have no effect.

REQ-API-003 Every JSON success is a HAL representation Tested 5/5 covered

Every successful response that carries a JSON body SHALL be served as application/hal+json, with its business data at the root and _links as a sibling member. Token issuance, token regeneration and the liveness probe are such representations. Stored content keeps its own media type, an empty or redirect response carries no JSON body, and the published OpenAPI document is the only JSON response outside this rule.

REQ-API-004 `_links.self` names what the representation is about Tested 5/5 covered

Every representation SHALL carry _links.self, a relative URI reference. It SHALL name the canonical URI of the resource the representation is about, even when the request used an alias, and the addressed resource when the representation reports an action on one. A representation of an operation with no addressed resource, including a failure, SHALL name the operation's request path.

REQ-API-005 Related resources are published as links Tested 3/3 covered

A representation SHALL publish each relation its capability's specification declares as a named link, keyed by that relation's name. An identifier MAY remain at the root; the link is how the client navigates. _links SHALL NOT carry business data, and related resources SHALL NOT be nested under _embedded without a proven performance need; the catalog collections of REQ-API-016 record that need.

REQ-API-007 A paginated collection is navigable by link Tested 4/4 covered

A collection that paginates SHALL accept limit, defaulting to 20 and ranging from 1 to 100, and offset starting at 0; a value outside a bound SHALL answer 422 Unprocessable Content. _links.self SHALL name the active view with its filters and page preserved, next SHALL appear when more items follow, and prev when the page does not start at the first item.

REQ-API-008 Every failure uses one envelope Tested 3/3 covered

Every failure other than a content-serving outcome SHALL be served as application/hal+json with the error message at the root and _links.self naming the request path without its query. The envelope SHALL cover use-case errors, authentication failures, routing fallbacks, extractor rejections, method rejections and body-limit failures. The content-serving outcomes 206, 304 and 416 belong to library/assets and carry no envelope.

An error envelope SHALL preserve the headers the protocol requires: Allow on 405 Method Not Allowed, WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on every 401 Unauthorized, and Retry-After on 429 Too Many Requests. Rewriting the body SHALL NOT drop them.

No generated document SHALL be committed.

REQ-API-016 A catalog collection embeds partial items Tested 5/5 covered

A catalog collection SHALL embed each page item's partial representation under _embedded.items and SHALL NOT repeat it at the root. Each embedded item SHALL carry _links.self, the cover relation its capability declares, and the browse fields — identifier, name and cover image identifier. The detail route SHALL return the full representation.

REQ-API-017 Date and time properties declare their wire format Tested 3/3 covered

Every date property, in a request or a response, SHALL declare format: date in YYYY-MM-DD; every timestamp property SHALL declare format: date-time in RFC 3339 UTC. No date or timestamp property SHALL be published without its format. A request value that does not match its declared format SHALL answer 422 Unprocessable Content, and a response value SHALL render in the declared format.

REQ-AUTHENTICATION-008 Login is rate limited per client address and account Tested 6/6 covered

Login SHALL be limited both per client address and per user account. The account key SHALL be the resolved user identifier; an identifier that resolves to no account SHALL use a derived key that does not reveal it. An attempt SHALL be rejected when either key is exhausted, answering 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. Both keys SHALL use the configured burst and period. The client address SHALL be the peer unless it is a configured trusted proxy, whose declared header is then read.

30 requirements · 84 scenarios · 70 covered (83%) · 14 uncovered · 20 Rust-only

REQ-AUTHORIZATION-001 Every authorizable entity is a resource Partial 1/3 covered

The system SHALL model every authorizable entity as a resource: a surrogate identifier, a resource kind, an optional owner, an optional authorization parent, and a visibility. The system SHALL resolve the kind, owner and parent from stored state, and SHALL never trust a client-supplied kind, owner or parent. A resource that does not exist SHALL be indistinguishable from one the caller may not discover.

REQ-AUTHORIZATION-002 The resource tree defines authorization parents Partial 3/6 covered

The authorization parent SHALL be the single canonical permission-inheritance edge. Each capability SHALL declare the authorization parent of the resources it defines. The resource tree SHALL be the one drawn by the PlantUML diagram in docs/Permissions.md § Resource tree; that diagram is the canonical picture, and this requirement states the rule rather than a second copy of the edges.

REQ-AUTHORIZATION-003 Containment and reference edges lend read access only Tested 5/5 covered

A resource relation SHALL be AlbumMember, PlaylistEntry or GroupMember. It SHALL lend Discover, ViewMetadata, View and Stream from its container to the target and the target's authorization-parent descendants. It SHALL NOT lend Download, a write, a share or an admin action, SHALL NOT become an authorization parent, and SHALL lose to a Deny.

REQ-AUTHORIZATION-004 Authorization parents are single, acyclic and bounded Not tested 0/3 covered

A resource SHALL have at most one authorization parent. Assigning one SHALL reject a cycle, and a decision SHALL NOT walk more than 32 authorization-parent edges. An assignment that would create a cycle or exceed the bound SHALL apply nothing.

REQ-AUTHORIZATION-007 Read actions distinguish discovery, metadata, content, stream and download Tested 2/2 covered

Discover SHALL report that a resource exists and include it in a listing. ViewMetadata SHALL read its metadata without its content. View SHALL read its rendered content. The system SHALL resolve the complete configuration from the built-in defaults, then the settings the configuration file names, then the settings the environment names, in that order of increasing precedence. Every setting SHALL have a built-in default, so an absent, empty or partial file still yields a complete configuration.

REQ-DOWNLOAD-001 Content requires the session credential Tested 3/3 covered

Every content route SHALL authenticate its request with Authorization: Bearer and SHALL decide that request as it arrives. A request without a valid session token SHALL answer 401 Unauthorized and read no bytes. The system SHALL NOT accept a credential supplied in the query string, and no representation SHALL publish one.

REQ-DOWNLOAD-005 Content supports byte ranges Tested 5/5 covered

The system SHALL advertise Accept-Ranges: bytes on every content response and SHALL answer a request carrying one Range: bytes= header with 206 Partial Content, a Content-Range header and only the requested bytes. A closed range, an open-ended range and a suffix range SHALL be supported. A range the content cannot satisfy SHALL answer 416 Range Not Satisfiable with Content-Range: bytes */<size>. A request naming more than one range SHALL be answered with the whole content.

A request whose If-Range does not match the content SHALL answer the whole content instead of a partial one.

REQ-FILE-001 A stored file records one stored content Tested 3/3 covered

A Stored file SHALL record one content stored under the Library root, addressed by a path relative to that root, carrying its media type, its size in bytes, the instant its content was last modified, the date it was registered, its origin and whether it is public. Origin SHALL be UPLOADED when the server received the content through upload and SCANNED when it found the content under the root.

REQ-GALLERY-003 Create a gallery Tested 5/5 covered

Creating a gallery SHALL require the CreateChild action on GALLERY_COLLECTION. The name SHALL be non-empty, at most 100 characters, and SHALL NOT begin or end with whitespace; such a name answers 422 and stores nothing. Interior whitespace is allowed and the submitted value is stored unchanged. is_public SHALL default to false. A duplicate name for the same owner SHALL answer 409 Conflict; success SHALL answer 201 Created with a Location.

The security-event catalog:

Event Severity Fields Recorded when
input_validation_failed warn field, reason a client-supplied value fails validation in a handler or use case
enum_validation_failed warn field, reason a discrete, finite list (for example Role) rejects a value
output_validation_failed warn reason stored data fails to decode, or an integrity check fails
authn_succeeded info actor a credential is accepted
authn_failed warn reason a credential is rejected; one reason, never distinguishing a bad identity from a bad secret
authz_failed warn actor, action, target an authorization decision denies an action
session_validation_failed warn reason a token is missing, invalid or expired
rate_limit_exceeded warn route, reason a request is rejected by a rate limiter
limit_exceeded warn source, reason a request body or query string exceeds a configured size limit
metadata_provider_fallback warn provider, classification a metadata provider is skipped because of a classified failure
metadata_provider_unconfigured warn provider a lookup names a metadata provider that is not configured
metadata_genre_unmatched debug count a metadata provider reports a genre outside the shared vocabulary
metadata_artwork_failed warn provider, reason artwork a provider reports cannot be downloaded or accepted
deserialization_failed warn source, reason a JSON body or the configuration fails to deserialize
extractor_fault error reason an inbound extractor rejects a request for a server-side fault
ingest info registered, completed, untouched, changed, missing, removed, skipped a library ingest operation (scan or observed change) finishes; never a file name or path
ingest_fault warn kind, operation the change observer degraded (a failed watch registration, a watcher error or overflow)
application_error error operation a use case originates an internal Unknown
port_fault error kind, operation an outbound adapter maps a dependency failure
constraint_rejected warn kind, operation an outbound adapter maps an expected constraint to a business result
token_provider_fault error kind the inbound token boundary receives an operational fault from the token provider
lifecycle info component, outcome startup, shutdown or logging initialization
user_admin info actor, action, target a user is created, updated or deleted, a role or credential changes
secret_initialized info component the pepper or the signing secret is generated when the instance identity is created
credential_rotated info actor a password is replaced or rehashed
token_regenerated info actor a caller regenerates its access token
upload info actor, upload, outcome an upload is accepted, a chunk written, an upload completed or cancelled
upload_reap info expired, orphaned, unsealed an upload reaping run finishes; aggregate counts only, never a file name or path
suspicious_business_logic warn actor, action, reason an action is out of order, nonsensical in context, or exceeds a limit
sensitive_data_access debug actor, object a request reads personal data
system_object info object, action a system-level object is created (the instance identity, the Root Admin)
unexpected_http_method warn method, path a request uses a method the route does not support

The authz_failed fields are a closed vocabulary shared with the permission catalog: action is one of read, moderate, manage, use, write, update, update_role, create, delete or patch_credential; target is one of library, gallery, playlist, file, upload or user.

Events with no surface in this server are deliberately absent: import/export, network and TLS failures, payment, geolocation and consent, fraud, excessive use, and key rotation.

 Business rule System suite

Every Stored file SHALL be addressed by a path relative to a single Library root that is a fixed location, and SHALL NOT be addressed by an absolute path. A file the server stored and a file it found already present SHALL be addressed the same way, so one root resolves every registered file.

REQ-MEDIA-INGEST-002 An absent library root is decided at startup Tested 4/4 covered

The server SHALL NOT create the Library root. When it is absent at startup the server SHALL wait up to the library.startup.media_root_wait_seconds window for it to appear and SHALL run the scan if it does. When it is still absent after the window, the server SHALL refuse startup when library.startup.fail_without_media_root is true, and otherwise start and reconcile the library as empty.

REQ-METADATA-ENRICHMENT-024 An apply resolves the reference and writes authoritatively Partial 5/6 covered

The system SHALL resolve the request's reference through its provider and write the reported metadata in one transaction: every field the provider reports SHALL replace the stored value, and a value it does not report SHALL be cleared. A reference that cannot be resolved, resolves another kind, or fails SHALL write nothing. The write SHALL name the EditMetadata action on the addressed entry.

Creating a film SHALL require the CreateChild action on the catalogue with the film child kind. An unknown genre SHALL be stored on demand. A new film SHALL answer 201 Created with a Location; a film already backed by that video 200; a video already attached elsewhere 409; a denied caller 403.

Updating a film SHALL require View and then EditMetadata on the film through PATCH /api/v1/library/movie/{movie_id}. An absent field SHALL keep its stored value and null SHALL clear an optional one. A supplied name SHALL be non-empty, at most 100 characters, and SHALL NOT begin or end with whitespace; the submitted value is stored unchanged. The backing video SHALL NOT change. An unknown or unviewable film SHALL answer 404; a readable film the caller may not edit 403; an unusable value 422 or 409.

A film SHALL be a resource under the catalogue, whose authorization parent SHALL be the catalogue. It SHALL have no owner. A read SHALL follow View and Stream, and a write SHALL follow EditMetadata, ReplaceMedia, CreateChild and Delete granted on the film or the catalogue. A Standard User SHALL NOT edit a film by default.

A read SHALL follow View and Stream, and a write SHALL follow EditMetadata, ReplaceMedia, CreateChild and Delete granted on the resource or an ancestor. A Standard User SHALL NOT edit a catalogue music resource by default.

REQ-SERIES-008 A show is created Tested 6/6 covered

Creating a show SHALL require the CreateChild action on the catalogue with the show child kind. The request SHALL name a name that is non-empty, at most 100 characters and does not begin or end with whitespace, and optional plot, first air date, country of origin, genres and cover; the submitted name is stored unchanged. An unknown genre SHALL be stored on demand. A new show SHALL answer 201 Created with a Location; a repeated name SHALL create a second show. Unusable input SHALL answer 422; a non-library cover 409; a denied caller 403.

REQ-STATE-006 A missing state for an existing datastore fails startup Tested 4/4 covered

When the datastore exists and no state is persisted, the system SHALL refuse to start and SHALL NOT create a replacement state. The datastore's presence SHALL be decided without treating an unreadable path as absent; an undecidable presence SHALL fail startup.

REQ-UPLOAD-015 Expired, stale and orphaned sessions are reaped Tested 5/5 covered

Definitions

Covered
A committed system case, an API-suite entry or a Rust // proves: claim.
Proof source
Each scenario counts once by its strongest evidence: system suite, then API suite, then Rust, then a Cause (Skipped). A scenario with none is Uncovered. A scenario with several proofs shows only its strongest source in the bar.
Why not black box
An authored memo explaining why a Rust proof stands in for a black-box case. It does not affect coverage.
Covered / Skipped / Uncovered
Covered: a system, API or Rust proof. Skipped: no proof but a non-empty Cause. Uncovered: no proof and no Cause.
Cause
An authored reason a scenario is skipped. A Cause marks a scenario with no proof as Skipped; it does not add a proof.
Note
Free-form authored commentary. It never affects coverage or the Skipped mark.
Requirement status
Tested: every declared scenario is covered. Partial: some are. Not tested: none is.
N/A
Authored in the JSON, marking a type the requirement does not exercise. A proof behind an N/A cell is a contradiction and is reported above.
